title: Knockback
subtitle: Build a readable knockback with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
overview: A hit displaces the player, so its real danger depends on nearby walls, ledges, hazards, and the loss of a chosen position.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a knockback as one rule.

demo.title: Test the knockback
phaseDescriptions: Communicate push direction and strength through the boss pose, impact line, and arena context before the force resolves.
Players brace, move away from dangerous boundaries, steer during displacement, use immunity, or deliberately take a safe push for repositioning.
The player regains control before the next unavoidable threat while the boss completes its follow-through, preserving recovery from a safe landing.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Communicate push direction and strength through the boss pose, impact line, and arena context before the force resolves.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Players brace, move away from dangerous boundaries, steer during displacement, use immunity, or deliberately take a safe push for repositioning.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The player regains control before the next unavoidable threat while the boss completes its follow-through, preserving recovery from a safe landing.

mistakes.title: A small-looking hit that launches the player farther than the arena reads makes environmental deaths feel arbitrary
mistakes.body: A small-looking hit that launches the player farther than the arena reads makes environmental deaths feel arbitrary.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible knockback cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Evaluate force, stun time, air control, collision behavior, and every possible landing zone rather than balancing damage alone.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Combine moderate push with changing boundary hazards or directional choices instead of scaling force until recovery is impossible.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The player regains control before the next unavoidable threat while the boss completes its follow-through, preserving recovery from a safe landing.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A hit displaces the player, so its real danger depends on nearby walls, ledges, hazards, and the loss of a chosen position. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Players brace, move away from dangerous boundaries, steer during displacement, use immunity, or deliberately take a safe push for repositioning. Evaluate force, stun time, air control, collision behavior, and every possible landing zone rather than balancing damage alone.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: A small-looking hit that launches the player farther than the arena reads makes environmental deaths feel arbitrary. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
At least one route remains reachable with the movement options available at this point.
Position and timing trade easier clearance against a better recovery opportunity.
